---
title: Study population and sampling
---

## Sampling procedure

The GIFT study began with a patient inception cohort survey (PIC Survey)
from which we determined eligibility for the clinical intervention
trial. Georgia and California SEER registry leads at Emory University
and University of Southern California identified an inception cohort of
eligible patients (via Information Management Services Calverton MD @Katz_2025_25_366)
aged 18 and older, diagnosed with a broad array of cancers in 2018-2019,
who linked (via the ongoing Georgia California Genetic Testing Linkage
Initiative @Katz_2025_25_366) to germline testing, and who were found to have a
pathogenic variant (PV) in one of 27 cancer susceptibility genes and
were alive at the time of selection (n=4300). 

**Supplemental Table 1** lists the genes included in the study, grouped by cancer susceptibility
and guidelines for prevention and control at the time of selection of
the patient sample.(@Daly_2021_19_77) The SEER registries provided a third-party
honest broker, Information Management Services, Inc. (IMS; the honest
broker for the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Surveillance Program),
with the de-identified clinical datasets maintained by the registries
from the Georgia California Genetic Testing Linkage Initiative. IMS
sampled an inception cohort of patients from this file using both
clinical and genetic test result data according to the study eligibility
criteria. IMS "salted" the sample with an additional 5% patients who did
not link to a test result, which ensured that registry field teams did
not know whether a given patient was tested or not, nor the result of
any genetic test. After salting, IMS returned the patient IDs of the
sampled individuals to the respective registry, with no information
regarding genetic test status. Inclusion criteria for the Patient
Inception Cohort (PIC) survey and subsequent invitation to the trial
were given in the main text.  

**Supplemental Table 2** lists the enrolled population characteristics
